prompts: The game went down in June and we owe the team an incident report. The logs and their notes are in {WS}/logs. When did it start and end, how long was it, did we keep our monthly availability target, and why did it happen? Record it in {WS}/result.json: start, end, minutes_down, availability_june_pct, slo_999_ok, root_cause.
answers:
[goal] June incident report in result.json.

[action] Read logs/README.md (down = first save error → 'server ready'; SLO 99.9%; one incident) and all three June logs. Grepped for ERROR/WARN/FATAL/'server ready'. Found the incident in gameserver-2026-06-02.log: disk /data at 97% (03:10:02), SaveGame "No space left on device" at 03:17:42, FATAL watchdog restart loop (exit 137) until backup rotation freed 38.2 GB at 03:52:10, then "server ready" at 03:53:31. June 1's only error (RCON auth failure) is not a save error and the server never went down. June 3 has no errors. Computed duration and availability with python.

[result] ./result.json:
- start: 2026-06-02 03:17:42 (first SaveGame failure)
- end: 2026-06-02 03:53:31 (server ready)
- minutes_down: 35.8 (2149 s = 35.8167 min)
- availability_june_pct: 99.9171 ((30×1440 − 35.8167) / 43200)
- slo_999_ok: true (99.9171 ≥ 99.9)
- root_cause: /data disk filled up → save writes failed → watchdog crash-looped the server until backup rotation freed space.

Assumptions: "down" follows the README's definition (first save error to server ready); availability uses the full 30-day month (43200 min) with the single incident; the 09:12:40 RCON auth error on June 1 is not a save error and does not start an incident.

[evidence] Log lines 241, 251, 253, 292, 294 of gameserver-2026-06-02.log quoted above; python output: down_min 35.8167, avail_pct 99.9171. No browser tabs, windows or apps were opened.
